In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BPI recognizes the lipid A portion of LPS and that the long-chain LPS of smooth strains of Proteus and Escherichio coli are less accessible to BPI.
long-chain LPS of smooth strains of P. Mirabilis are responsible for the high resistance to holo-Bpi.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BPI is a very effective antibacterial agent against gram-negative bacteria with Re-LPS.
the BPI resistance of Proteus and E. coli is due to the length of the polysaccharide chain, which is the major determinant for the structure of LPS in these bacteria.
the BPI resistance of smooth bacteria is not due to the structural diversity of their lipid A but rather to the presence of long polysac-charide chains in the LPS envelope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BPI recognizes LPS in a manner that is independent of the chain length of the polysaccharide.
BPI recognizes LPS in the outer membrane, not in solution.
BPI is a potent and selective antibacterial protein that can kill a variety of gram-negative bacteria, including some that are highly resistant to other antibiotics.
